entities.name: Ignazio Masotti
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Ignazio Masotti (1814–1888) was an Italian cardinal of the late nineteenth century who served the Roman Curia under Pius IX and Leo XIII. Rising through curial congregations concerned with discipline, religious orders, and administration, he belonged to the bureaucracy that managed the Church after the loss of the Papal States in 1870.

Masotti’s generation confronted the ‘Roman Question’, anticlerical liberal states, and the need to govern a globalising Catholic missionary and educational apparatus without temporal sovereignty. Leo XIII’s intellectual and diplomatic turn still required hard-working curial cardinals to run congregations day to day.

He is best understood as an administrative pillar of the Leonine Curia—evidence that papal recovery after 1870 rested as much on clerical bureaucracy as on encyclicals and nunciatures.
